A1.justification: Both readable ten-page PDFs describe the same RAD research, with inspectable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement, although both refer to supplementary material.

before.justification: v1 reports original RAD inpainting scores, inference timings, FFHQ ablations and qualitative results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports quantitative ImageNet comparisons in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same spatially variant diffusion formulation, two-phase Perlin-mask schedules, spatial noise embedding, inverse timestep mapping and LoRA adaptation. No proposed algorithmic component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use FFHQ, LSUN Bedroom and ImageNet with box, extreme and wide inpainting masks. ImageNet already appears in v1's experimental settings and Figure 4; its added numerical scores quantify existing coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain their comparator methods, and Figure 4 still compares RAD with RePaint and MCG. The new ImageNet columns reuse Table 1's existing quantitative baseline set. GradPaint is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 changes the stated ImageNet training length from 800K to 700K. The validation sample count, image resolution, mask definitions, batch sizes and sampling procedure remain unchanged. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The two FFHQ component ablations in Table 3 and Figure 6, diversity examples in Figure 5, and observations about mask blurring and noise scheduling in Section 3.2 are retained. No new diagnostic or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added ImageNet entries follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds a full quantitative ImageNet comparison. RAD's FID/LPIPS values are 47.0/0.118 for box, 57.8/0.374 for extreme and 56.7/0.104 for wide masks, best among the reported methods in all six columns. This substantially expands numerical evidence beyond v1's qualitative ImageNet examples. Existing FFHQ/LSUN scores, timings and ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the spatially variant Gaussian formulation, reasoning about spatial dependence, and the no-noise special case are unchanged. No additional proof or substantive mathematical derivation appears in the supplied PDFs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions, three-dataset performance claims and up-to-100-times inference speed claim. The added ImageNet numbers support an existing claim rather than changing its scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the ablations and weaker DDNM/DeqIR performance remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning explicit training, dependence on mask distributions and potentially better RePaint/MCG results in extreme cases.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly specifies ImageNet exponential moving averaging with decay 0.999 and revises its reported training length to 700K. The PDFs do not establish whether EMA was newly introduced or merely newly documented. Other implementation and hardware details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Grechka et al.'s GradPaint as reference 10 and cites it among ADM-based inpainting methods in Section 2. The remaining cited works and substantive research positioning are retained after renumbering.

P1.justification: v4 updates author affiliations and contact information, expands ADM to 'ablated diffusion models', makes small editorial corrections and adds acknowledgments. The main prose, section order and narrative remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains ImageNet columns, smaller text and additional separators. The author block and figures are compacted, Figures 2–3 switch columns, and Tables 2–3 move. All six figures retain their visual content. Table 1's caption still names only FFHQ and LSUN Bedroom.

improvement.justification: The new ImageNet quantitative comparison strengthens support for the existing three-dataset performance claim, while the EMA disclosure improves reproducibility information. These are useful but limited gains because the method and diagnostic analyses remain unchanged. The expanded table is denser and retains an outdated caption, a small presentation drawback.
